sources.entry: statsforecast - Fast statistical forecasting models such as ARIMA, ETS, and Theta, compiled with numba.

summary.one_liner: StatsForecast is a Python library of univariate time series forecasting models (AutoARIMA, AutoETS, AutoCES, Theta, MSTL and others) built for fast fitting on large collections of series.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a collection of univariate forecasting models including automatic ARIMA, ETS, CES and Theta, plus a large set of benchmark models. Models are used through a StatsForecast class with sklearn-style .fit and .predict methods, and predictions can include point forecasts and prediction intervals at chosen confidence levels. Supported model families listed in the README include ARIMA/AutoRegressive, Theta variants, MSTL/MFLES/TBATS for multiple seasonalities, GARCH and ARCH for volatility, baselines (Naive, HistoricAverage, SeasonalNaive and others), exponential smoothing (Simple, Holt, HoltWinters), and intermittent-demand models (ADIDA, Croston variants, IMAPA, TSB). The README says some models accept exogenous variables and that the library offers anomaly detection based on in-sample prediction intervals. It also states it can run on Spark, Dask and Ray for large numbers of series.
use_cases: forecast many univariate time series in production
detect anomalies in time series using prediction intervals
forecast electricity load with multiple seasonalities
how_to_run: from statsforecast import StatsForecast; from statsforecast.models import AutoARIMA
notable: Automatic model selection for ARIMA, ETS, CES and Theta across many series at once
Large battery of benchmark and intermittent-demand models in one package
Probabilistic forecasts and in-sample prediction intervals
Scales to millions of series with Spark, Dask or Ray according to the README
caveats: Performance claims (for example 20x faster than pmdarima, 1.5x faster than R) are stated in the README and not independently verified here
Scaling to distributed backends is described as out-of-the-box but requires those frameworks to be set up separately
